conventions.convention: A Hermitian matrix supplies a real symmetric zero-one off-diagonal support matrix; symbolic elimination uses that matrix, while numerical Schur complements use the original Hermitian matrix.
Ordering positions are zero-based. Row j of P is row v_j of the identity, so B=PAP* has B_ij=A_(v_i,v_j). Factor entries use ordered coordinates.
A structural column contains its pivot and its later filled neighbors. Reach includes the starting vertex; ancestors require one or more parent edges.
Coordinate nested dissection splits every coordinate side of length at least two at its lower median, orders child boxes first, and appends the union of separator hyperplanes lexicographically.
The LU growth parameter is the maximum magnitude over all active matrices divided by the original maximum entry magnitude; it is not merely the maximum entry of U divided by that magnitude.

The Hermitian kernel separates rounded real-component numerical arithmetic from a finite-budget exact real controller. Unresolved pivot certificates return pivot-inconclusive; nonzero out-of-normal intermediates return range-failure.

Trailing-update residual bounds use conceptual exact multipliers. Actual stored-factor reconstruction additionally includes multiplier coupling residuals and uses stored-multiplier transformation growth.

Grid storage bounds count allocated factor entries, including structural zeros, and exclude temporary contribution arrays. Pattern equality for Cholesky requires every permitted recurrence numerator to be nonzero.

load_bearing.statement: For distinct remaining vertices x,y in V_k, {x,y} is an edge of G_k if and only if the original graph contains a finite walk from x to y whose internal vertices belong to {v_0,...,v_(k−1)}.
Every later filled neighbor of v_k lies on its parent path and is therefore an ancestor. If v_s is a child of v_k, then C_s minus {v_s} is contained in C_k.

For a Hermitian matrix, a fixed ordering and nonzero scalar pivots, the stated Schur updates preserve Hermitian symmetry, and every nonzero off-diagonal entry is an edge of the corresponding filled graph.

Under exact arithmetic, a Hermitian positive-definite input and a successful ordered multifrontal factorization, fronts produce the scalar Cholesky factor; assembly and scalar updates cost O(sum d_r²), symbolic factor allocation has exactly sum d_r positions, and each triangular solve costs O(sum d_r).

Every accepted kernel pivot is nonsingular and passes the exact componentwise threshold test. The displayed explicit coefficients bound multiplier error, trailing Schur error and the full reconstruction residual, including stored-multiplier coupling errors.

For a separator vertex v of recursion box B, every later filled neighbor lies in S_B union the exterior grid boundary of B; when every side has length at most s, its column size is at most 3d s^(d−1).

For real symmetric positive-definite grid-subgraph matrices with n=k^d, coordinate nested dissection gives O(n^(3/2)) work and O(n log n) factor storage in dimension two, and O(n²) work and O(n^(4/3)) factor storage in dimension three; k=1 has constant work and storage.

concerns.concern: The symbolic update says: “let N(J_r) be the union of the active graph neighbors of the vertices in J_r; remove J_r and connect every pair of distinct vertices in N(J_r).” For an internally adjacent two-vertex pivot block, this union includes the pivot vertices themselves. For example, J_r={0,1} with edge {0,1} gives N(J_r)={0,1}, so the literal instruction connects vertices just removed. The neighbor union needs restriction to remaining vertices. The intended correction is immediate and does not affect the displayed numerical Schur update.

The Statement writes its work and exact allocation sums over r=1,...,n, although the supplying algorithm defines F_r and pivot position r over 0,...,n−1. Thus d_n is undefined and d_0 is omitted. Use the established zero-based range, or explicitly reindex the column sizes.

The kernel lemma imports the supplier's length-j dot argument for j≤2, whose rounding condition follows from u<1, without imposing an unnecessary trailing-dimension restriction.
